description: Snowflake higher-order functions with lambda arguments: TRANSFORM(<arr>, x -> ...), FILTER(<arr>, x -> <bool>) and REDUCE(<arr>, <init>, (acc, x) -> ...). The lambda body is applied per element with the parameter bound as VARIANT, so arithmetic over it is FLOAT - x + 1 over [1,2,3] yields [2.000000000000000e+00,3.000000000000000e+00,4.000000000000000e+00]. A lambda parameter may DECLARE a type, which is not decoration: it CASTS the bound element and therefore changes that arithmetic, live-verified - TRANSFORM([1,2], a -> a * 2) is [2.000000000000000e+00,4.000000000000000e+00] while TRANSFORM([1,2], a INT -> a * 2) is [2,4]. TRANSFORM and FILTER take a ONE-parameter lambda; the index-carrying two-parameter form is not Snowflake syntax and is refused, while REDUCE's two-parameter lambda stays valid. Converted 1:1 from functions/HigherOrderFunctionTest (now retired); the Java class read the ARRAY cell's toString with whitespace stripped. TO_VARCHAR prints a DOUBLE element in the fifteen-decimal exponent form, and that spelling is what carries the FLOAT claim.

steps.sql: SELECT REPLACE(TO_VARCHAR(TRANSFORM(FILTER([1, 2, 3, 4], x -> x > 1), y -> y * 10)), ' ', '')
